name: The Bug Filer
oneLiner: Files a typed, deduplicated ADO Bug work item per test failure — title, repro steps, severity, screenshot, parent link — in one pass.
lead: Consumes a `TestFailure[]` from your runner and files each failure as a fully-populated Azure DevOps Bug via the REST API. Every field is set — title, description table, `Microsoft.VSTS.TCM.ReproSteps`, severity, priority, tags — the screenshot is attached, and the bug is linked under its parent user story. Idempotent: it searches for an existing open bug before creating.
chore: Manual triage means opening the tracker and hand-keying each failure into a new ticket: title, error, repro steps, severity, browser, screenshot, parent link. Across a dozen failures it's slow, and fatigue produces vague titles, missing screenshots, and duplicate filings.
instead: One consistently-structured Bug work item per failure, filed the moment it lands — identical field layout every time, no duplicates, no blank fields. Severity and priority are assigned by deterministic keyword rules, so the same failure always grades the same way.
whyItMatters: A clearly-written bug filed instantly gets fixed sooner. A vague or forgotten one regresses to production. Deterministic filing removes the human variance that lets that happen.

howItWorks.step: Iterates the `TestFailure[]` and, per failure, branches to create, update, or skip — then returns a tallied `AgentResponse`.
howItWorks.explain: The orchestrator. Failures are processed sequentially, not in parallel, so the dedup gate stays consistent — two failures of the same test in one batch can't race and both file a bug. For each, `findExistingBug` runs first; a match routes to `updateBug` (append a recurrence note) or a plain skip based on `updateExisting`, and the `continue` guarantees it never also creates. Only a genuine miss reaches `createBug`. `dryRun` is the safety valve: the full decide path runs, the write doesn't — so CI can preview the exact create/update/skip breakdown before anything touches the board.

howItWorks.step: Runs a WIQL query for an open Bug whose title already contains this test case and browser — the dedup gate.
howItWorks.explain: The dedup gate, written in WIQL — ADO's SQL-like work-item query language, available only over POST `/wit/wiql`. The dedup key is deliberately `testCase` **and** `browser`: the same test failing on two browsers files two bugs, because the repro differs. The `<> 'Closed'` / `<> 'Resolved'` clauses are the load-bearing part — an already-fixed bug is invisible to this query, so a **regression** files a fresh ticket instead of reopening stale history. WIQL returns ids only, so a hit costs a second `getBug` call to hydrate the title and URL. One caveat it exposes: `failure.testCase` is interpolated straight into the query, so titles are normalized upstream — an unescaped quote would break the WIQL.

howItWorks.step: Grades severity from keywords in the test case and error text — deterministic, no LLM.
howItWorks.explain: Deterministic severity mapping — no LLM, no heuristics that drift. It lowercases the test name and error, then checks keyword tiers in priority order and returns on the first match: `smoke`/`critical` in the test name short-circuits to `1 - Critical` (a smoke failure blocks everything downstream); a `navigate`/`login`/`auth` test or a `timeout` error → `2 - High`; `regression` → `3 - Medium`; everything else falls through to `4 - Low`. Order matters — first match wins, so a 'critical login smoke' test grades Critical, not High. Because it's pure keyword matching, the same failure grades identically across runs and machines, which is what makes the filed severities auditable.

howItWorks.step: Assembles the typed `BugDetails` — title, description, repro steps, severity, priority, area/iteration path, tags.
howItWorks.explain: Assembles the entire work-item payload as one typed `BugDetails` object before any network call — so the create step is a straight serialize-and-POST with nothing computed inline. The title template is load-bearing: it's the exact string the dedup gate greps for, so it must stay stable — change it and `findExistingBug` stops matching and you get duplicates. `areaPath` routes the bug onto the right team's backlog; it prefers `ADO_AREA_PATH` and falls back to a `<project>\\MyTeam` default, so the same code drops into any project by setting one env var. Severity and priority come from the deterministic keyword graders, not from the caller — so a bug can't be accidentally mis-graded.

howItWorks.step: POSTs the JSON-Patch document to create the `$Bug`, then links the parent story and attaches the screenshot.
howItWorks.explain: The write. ADO work-item creation isn't a plain JSON POST — it's a JSON-Patch document (`application/json-patch+json`), an array of `add` ops keyed by field reference name (`System.Title`, `Microsoft.VSTS.TCM.ReproSteps`, `Microsoft.VSTS.Common.Severity`…), sent to the `$Bug` work-item-type endpoint. Tags are joined with `; ` because that's ADO's on-the-wire delimiter. The bug is created in one call; the parent link and screenshot are two follow-up calls that only fire when there's a story id or an attachment — so a failure with no screenshot still files cleanly. The screenshot is what turns 'the test failed' into a triageable bug, which is the entire reason to do this automatically.

howItWorks.step: On a dedup hit with `updateExisting`, POSTs a timestamped comment to the existing bug instead of filing a duplicate.
howItWorks.explain: The 'seen it again' path. Instead of filing a duplicate, it POSTs an HTML comment to the matched bug's `comments` endpoint, stamping the recurrence with an ISO timestamp, the browser, and the error. The error runs through `escapeHtml` first — failure messages are untrusted text that routinely contain `<`/`>` from selectors or markup, and unescaped they'd corrupt the comment HTML. Keeping every recurrence on one work item is what makes 'this bug has failed 14 times since Tuesday' answerable — fragmenting it across duplicates destroys that signal. The `comments` API is still `-preview`, so the version is pinned deliberately.

examples.caption: Smoke test times out on mobile Safari
examples.input: `TestFailure`: testCase `mobile-login-smoke`, browser `mobile Safari`, error `Timed out waiting for the Sign In button`, plus a screenshot path.
examples.output: New Bug `[Automation] mobile-login-smoke failed on mobile Safari`, graded `1 - Critical` (the `smoke` keyword), tagged `mobile`, screenshot attached, linked under the Login story.

examples.caption: Same failure recurs mid-sprint
examples.input: A repeat of a test that already has an open bug from Monday, run with `--update-existing`.
examples.output: WIQL dedup hits the existing bug; instead of a duplicate it POSTs a timestamped comment — browser, error, ISO time — appending to the recurrence history on that one work item.

examples.caption: Low-severity CSS regression
examples.output: New Bug graded `4 - Low` (no critical/high/regression keywords) with repro steps, linked under the Profile story — filed without inflating the priority queue.

underHood.heading: Authenticates to the ADO REST API
underHood.input: The `TestFailure` — test case, browser, error, optional screenshot.
underHood.output: PAT-authenticated calls to the Azure DevOps work-item REST API (v7.0).

underHood.heading: WIQL dedup gate
underHood.output: An existing open Bug (title `CONTAINS` both terms) or null — the branch that prevents double-filing.

underHood.heading: Keyword severity/priority grading
underHood.input: Lowercased test case and error text.
underHood.output: One of four severity/priority tiers, assigned deterministically — no LLM, no run-to-run drift.

underHood.heading: JSON-Patch create + link + attach
underHood.output: A new Bug work item, hierarchy-linked to its parent story, with the screenshot attached.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
An Azure DevOps org/project and a **PAT** with work-item write (create Bug) scope.
A `TestFailure[]` JSON array from your runner — `testCase`, `browser`, `error`, optional `screenshot` path.
No LLM key — severity and priority are deterministic keyword rules, not a model.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is TypeScript on Node. One-time per machine.
steps.firstRun: First time only, on a new machine.

steps.label: Clone and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the ADO client and helpers into `node_modules`.
steps.firstRun: Full install, a minute or two.
steps.rerun: No-op once installed, unless the dependency list changed.

steps.label: Export the ADO target (environment variables).
steps.cmd:
export ADO_ORGANIZATION=my-org
export ADO_PROJECT="My Project"
export ADO_PAT=your-access-token
export ADO_AREA_PATH="My Project\\MyTeam"   # optional
steps.why: Read at startup to resolve the org/project and authenticate. Swap them to retarget a different project.

steps.label: Dry-run to preview the create/skip decisions.
steps.cmd:
npm run ado:bugs -- \
  --story 4001 \
  --failures '[{"testCase":"login-smoke","browser":"chromium","error":"Timed out waiting for the Sign In button"}]' \
  --dry-run
steps.why: `--dry-run` runs the full WIQL-search and decide flow but suppresses the write — validates your `--failures` JSON shape first.

steps.label: Run for real.
steps.cmd:
npm run ado:bugs -- \
  --story 4001 \
  --failures '[{"testCase":"login-smoke","browser":"chromium","error":"Timed out waiting for the Sign In button"}]'
steps.why: Drops `--dry-run` and files one Bug per failure, severity/priority auto-graded.
steps.firstRun: Files a net-new Bug for every failure with no matching open bug.
steps.rerun: Same failure hits the WIQL dedup gate: skipped, or — with `--update-existing` — a timestamped comment instead of a duplicate.

steps.label: Open the filed bug.
steps.cmd:
# the agent prints each ticket's link to the console, e.g.:
# Created: #6002  https://dev.azure.com/my-org/My%20Project/_workitems/edit/6002
steps.why: No local artifact — the Bug work item on ADO is the output; the console prints its url.

inputs.name: --failures <json>
inputs.desc: `TestFailure[]` JSON — testCase, browser, error, optional screenshot path.

inputs.name: --story <id>
inputs.desc: Parent user story ID to hierarchy-link every new bug under.

inputs.name: --dry-run
inputs.desc: Run the search/decide flow but suppress the write.

inputs.name: --update-existing
inputs.desc: Comment on a dedup match instead of skipping it.

outputs.name: Bug work items
outputs.desc: Created (or commented-on) directly in ADO — no local files written.

outputs.name: console summary
outputs.desc: created / updated / skipped / errored counts, plus each new bug's url.

runbook.rerun: Idempotent by construction: each failure hits the WIQL dedup gate (open Bug whose title CONTAINS the test case and browser) before any write, so a repeat failure never becomes a duplicate — it's skipped, or appended as a comment under `--update-existing`.
runbook.integrate: Wire it as the terminal step of a CI test job: emit the runner's failures as JSON, pipe into `--failures`, set `--story` from the build's linked feature. Add `--update-existing` on nightly/regression runs so a flaky failure accretes history on one bug instead of piling up duplicates.

video.caption: A 2-3 minute screen recording: a `TestFailure` becomes a filed, linked ADO Bug, live.
script: Open a terminal beside the team's work board so viewers can watch the ticket appear.
Say: 'This agent turns a failed test straight into a properly filled-out bug ticket. Watch.'
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; one line on what Node is.
Run `npm install` (or note it's already done); explain it's grabbing the tracker client.
Show the `export ADO_ORGANIZATION / ADO_PROJECT / ADO_PAT` lines; say this is the only client-specific config.
Run the command with `--dry-run` first; point out it shows what it would file without touching the tracker.
Run it again without `--dry-run`; narrate as the console prints 'Created: #6002' with a link.
Switch to the browser, open that link — show the ticket's title, severity, repro steps, and screenshot already filled in.
Re-run the exact same failure; show it now says 'skipped-existing' instead of filing a duplicate.
Close: 'One failure, one clean ticket, no duplicates — every time.'
